title: Your Second Brain: NotebookLM for Teachers
author: Dominic Salles
summary: After meeting NotebookLM's cofounder Steven Johnson, Salles outlines 10 classroom applications grounded in source materials: curating source-grounded learning environments, generating study guides, facilitating conversational learning, accelerating organizational tasks, supporting multilingual analysis, teaching fact-checking, adapting explanations to comprehension levels, encouraging cross-disciplinary connections, using audio overviews, and exploring themes with mind maps. The tool keeps students bound to trusted sources while enabling dynamic exploration.
points: Teachers can upload course materials, texts, and readings; NotebookLM becomes an 'instant expert' bound to those sources only.
Audio overviews convert complex texts into 10-minute conversational summaries, accommodating auditory learners and on-the-go consumption.
Inline citations for every answer teach students to fact-check and jump to original sources, linking synthesis back to primary knowledge.
Source-grounding prevents students from outsourcing thinking to open-web searches while maintaining intellectual rigor.
Mind maps dynamically organize themes and characters, generating detailed cited essays when students click nodes.
quotes: You chose the sources you trust, and NotebookLM only uses those sources. You can upload all your PPTs, or your notes, or the sites you trust, the videos you trust, the text you are studying and let your students ask it anything they want.
Dialogue is a historically valuable and 'ancient way of understanding things'—conversational hypertext turns linear reading into a dynamic, non-linear exploratory process.
